help.address: Publicly address everyone or a selected character. Addressing is not private messaging. Everyone in this scene can still hear the contribution.
help.ambient: Names offered for your in-world contributions, such as Bystander or Anonymous voice. These labels are world content and are not translated with the app interface.
help.apiKey: Credential stored locally for this provider. Leave the field blank to retain an existing key. Credentials are not returned by the API or included in world save files.
help.attempt: Number of the latest attempt for this logical request. Values above 1 indicate a retry after a retryable failure. The app makes at most three attempts.
help.autoResume: When enabled, worlds that were running before shutdown restart their schedules after the backend boots. By default they return paused. Closing a browser never pauses a running world.
help.background: Personal history and private starting knowledge supplied only to this character. Other characters do not automatically receive it.
help.bannedPunctuation: Applies to newly generated prose in dialogue, narrator titles and reports, notable events, and private memories. Required JSON delimiters and addressing identifiers are exempt. Previously stored history is not rewritten.
help.baseUrl: Provider API root. Use the chat-completions API root for an OpenAI-compatible provider, or the Ollama server root for its native protocol. This is separate from the model ID.
help.cancelTime: Elapsed time from creating this logical request until Communion stopped it. It can include queue wait, model generation, and waiting for public delivery.
help.captureReasoning: Store reasoning text that the provider actually exposes. This is separate from displaying it in chat and from the provider's reasoning effort. Turning capture off does not make the model think less.
help.characterName: Name used to identify this person or reusable library entry. Character speech is attributed using the individual character's name.
help.characterPersonality: This individual's personality instructions. Characters can share a persona while keeping their own background, beliefs, goals, and memories.
help.characterPrompt: Shared character instructions combined with each person's own personality, background, memory, and setting. Preserve the structured speak/no_response output contract. Supported placeholders are shown below the editor.
help.characterSlots: Maximum concurrent character-generation requests within the total request limit. Keeping this below the total leaves capacity for memory and narrator requests.
help.compaction: Start first-person memory compaction at this percentage of the effective context budget. At 60, compaction begins around 60 percent full. The complete public transcript remains on disk.
help.contextCapacity: Configured model context capacity in tokens. Communion uses this value for budgeting and context estimates. It is a setting, not an automatic measurement of the provider's actual capacity.
help.contextPressure: Estimated input tokens divided by the provider profile's configured capacity. It is not an exact tokenizer count. Working-context ceilings and output reserves separately affect the engine's compaction budget.
help.cooldown: Minimum seconds after a model response before this character can request another turn. Silence also uses a cooldown. Provider latency and queued speech can make the actual interval longer.
help.finishReason: Provider-reported reason the stream ended. A length limit can indicate truncated output. Not recorded means the provider or old record did not supply a final reason.
help.firstToken: Time from the app starting this request until the first exposed reasoning or speech chunk. This includes queue wait. It is not necessarily the first visible speech token.
help.globalGap: Minimum seconds between public speech parts in one session, across all its characters. A value of 1 allows at most one delivered part per second. It does not set request frequency or individual character cooldowns.
help.globalRules: Instructions shared by every model request, across providers and worlds. They apply to speech, narration, memories, and other generated prose. The punctuation restrictions below are also checked before prose is accepted.
help.httpStatus: HTTP response code recorded from the provider. A 200 response can still be followed by cancellation or invalid model output. Not recorded means no response code was saved, not that the request succeeded.
help.inFlight: Requests in the recent diagnostic window that are queued, connecting, reasoning, receiving output, or waiting to retry. Queued requests may not yet have reached the provider.
help.includeTime: Include the projected time beside each public observation sent to characters. Full timestamps remain in storage regardless of this setting. This does not change the computer's clock.
help.interfaceLanguage: Language for application labels, help, and number/date formatting. It does not translate model prompts, character names, dialogue, memories, or scenario content.
help.keyEnv: Environment variable from which the backend reads this profile's key. AUTO searches supported local key variables for the default GLM profile. Restart the backend after editing .env.
help.lastFailure: Most recently recorded timeout, network, or HTTP failure for this request. It may describe an earlier retry even when a later attempt succeeded.
help.latency: Recorded request durations in completion order for the recent sample. Duration includes queue wait and provider processing. Missing timings are not treated as successful zero-duration calls.
help.logCharacter: Filter log entries to one character. Operator and narrator events may have no character ID and are hidden while this filter is active.
help.logLevel: Filter diagnostic entries by severity. DEBUG is detailed activity, INFO is normal lifecycle events, WARNING covers recoverable issues, and ERROR indicates a failed operation.
help.maxOutput: Maximum output-token allowance sent with each request, including reasoning tokens where the provider counts them. Too small an allowance can exhaust output before the model produces usable speech.
help.maxParts: Maximum number of parts delivered from one generated response. Words beyond this limit are discarded. Raising it allows longer speeches and a larger delivery queue.
help.meanLatency: Average recorded duration among recent requests with timing data. It includes local queue wait. It is a recent sample, not an average over the entire session.
help.memoryPrompt: Instructions for summarizing one character's observations into its own memory. Preserve first-person beliefs and attribution. This does not rewrite the public transcript.
help.memoryWords: Requested size of each character's retained first-person memory after compaction. It is a model instruction rather than an exact word count. Larger memories preserve more detail but consume more context.
help.model: Exact model identifier sent to the provider, such as glm-5.3. A display name alone does not select a different model.
help.narratorEnabled: Off by default. When enabled, the narrator prepares periodic reports while this session runs and has new speech. Generate recap is available on demand regardless of this switch. Reports remain operator-only.
help.narratorInterval: Minimum seconds between scheduled narrator recaps while this session runs and has new public speech. It does not control character turns. On-demand recaps can be requested separately.
help.narratorPrompt: Instructions controlling report style, notable-event selection, and evidence links. This prompt is used only for the operator's narrator, not for character dialogue.
help.narratorProvider: Provider profile used for narrator reports. It can differ from the profiles used by characters. Narration shares the backend's total request limit.
help.narratorScope: Public access reads the shared transcript. Private access may also read character memories and captured reasoning. Reports are always operator-only and are never fed back into characters.
help.observationCutoff: Highest public message ID included when this request took its observation snapshot. Messages arriving later were not visible to that generation. IDs are references, not message counts.
help.outcomes: Recent request outcomes, including errors, retries, and cancellations. The sample is limited to the requests currently loaded in diagnostics, not the full session history.
help.persona: Reusable personality traits. Applying a persona copies its instructions, not another character's identity or memory. Existing characters retain their own copy.
help.protocol: Request and streaming format used by the adapter. OpenAI-compatible uses chat completions, Ollama native uses its local chat format, and Mock laboratory generates local test responses without a model call.
help.provider: Model connection assigned to this character. Several characters can share a connection while keeping separate identities and memories.
help.providerConcurrency: Maximum concurrent requests using this provider profile, within the backend's total limit. A larger value does not override provider throttling.
help.providerName: Name used in Communion to identify this provider profile. The model ID and endpoint are configured separately.
help.providerReasoning: Only reasoning text returned by the provider is shown. It may be partial after cancellation or limited by storage settings. It is not an inspection of hidden internal model reasoning.
help.queueDelay: Time waiting for a free backend or provider concurrency slot before the HTTP request starts. High values can indicate that configured request slots are busy.
help.quiet: The character still receives observations and makes requests on its normal schedule, but generated speech is not published. This does not remove it from the world or stop request use.
help.reasoningEffort: Requested reasoning level for this provider. Low asks for less reasoning when supported. It does not disable thinking. Auto lets the provider choose. Capture and display settings do not change inference effort.
help.reasoningLimit: Maximum exposed reasoning text stored for a single request. Extra reasoning is not saved after this limit. This limits storage, not model thinking or provider token use.
help.reasoningPhase: Measured time from the first exposed reasoning chunk to the first speech chunk, or the stream end if no speech was returned. Providers that expose no reasoning may have no separate measurement.
help.recentErrors: Requests currently marked Error in the recent diagnostic window. Intentional silence, cancellation, and interrupted requests are separate outcomes.
help.requestConcurrency: Maximum model requests in flight across the backend, shared by character turns, memory compaction, and narration. Extra work waits in the queue. The provider can impose a lower limit.
help.requiresKey: Require a configured key before starting an OpenAI-compatible character connection. Local endpoints often do not require authentication.
help.role: Short public description visible in the character roster supplied to other characters. Keep private facts in the background field instead.
help.scenarioDescription: Short description shown in the scenario library. The shared opening premise is the setting sent to characters.
help.scenarioPremise: Shared starting situation and ongoing activity supplied to every character in a new session. Existing sessions keep their own copy when a scenario template is edited.
help.scenarioSelection: Reusable starting setting and cast for a new session. Creating a session makes a separate copy with its own history and character memories.
help.sessionName: Operator-facing name of this saved session. Leave it blank to use the scenario name. It does not rename the characters.
help.setting: Starting situation supplied to every character in a new session. It can describe any place or ongoing activity. Editing a template does not rewrite an existing session.
help.showReasoning: Add links beside model speech that open the private reasoning inspector. Character context never includes these operator controls.
help.speakAs: Choose who characters hear your contribution as. A character identity uses that character's name. Ambient voices use the labels defined by this scenario. Your operator identity is not included.
help.status: Current lifecycle state of this request. Hover the state badge for its meaning. Completed generation, deliberate no response, cancellation, and provider errors have different meanings.
help.status.Cancelled: Communion stopped this unfinished turn, for example when pausing or reconfiguring the session or stopping the backend. It is not the character choosing silence. Previously published speech remains in history.
help.status.Completed: The generation stream finished. Character speech may still be split and waiting for paced public delivery.
help.status.Configured: The profile has an available credential or does not require one. This does not guarantee that its endpoint or model has been tested.
help.status.Cooldown: The character is waiting until its next scheduled opportunity. It still hears public observations on the next request.
help.status.DeliveringSpeech: The response was generated and is waiting for paced public delivery. Other characters can speak between its parts.
help.status.Error: This operation failed, for example because of a network problem, timeout, provider rejection, or invalid output. Inspect the error and logs for details.
help.status.Idle: No active turn is currently being processed for this character. In a paused session this is normal.
help.status.Interrupted: The backend restarted before this request reached a known final state. The unfinished request is not replayed automatically.
help.status.NeedsKey: A required credential is unavailable. Configure the provider before starting its characters.
help.status.NoResponse: The character deliberately chose not to speak on this turn. No public message was posted. Its normal cooldown still applies.
help.status.Paused: Autonomous character turns are stopped. History and in-world operator contributions remain available. Resume restarts the schedule.
help.status.Queued: Waiting for a free concurrency slot. The provider may not have received the request yet.
help.status.Reasoning: The provider is returning exposed reasoning text. Public speech has not necessarily arrived yet.
help.status.ReceivingOutput: The provider is streaming output. It is validated before public speech is published.
help.status.Requesting: Connecting to the provider or waiting for its stream to start.
help.status.RetryWait: A retryable failure occurred. The backend is waiting before trying again.
help.status.Running: The backend is scheduling this session even if its browser view is closed.
help.status.interrupted: The backend restarted before this request reached a known final state. The unfinished request is not replayed automatically.
help.status.noResponse: The character deliberately chose not to speak on this turn. No public message was posted. Its normal cooldown still applies.
help.supportsEffort: Include reasoning_effort in requests sent through this provider profile. Enable only when the endpoint accepts that parameter.
help.timeout: HTTPX network timeout for connection and stream operations. A request can fail if the provider stalls beyond this interval. It is not a character cooldown or a guaranteed maximum length of a streamed response.
help.timezone: IANA time zone used for model-visible observation times, such as Asia/Bangkok. It does not change the host operating system time zone.
help.tokenUsage: Token counts reported by the provider when available. These differ from local context estimates. Output may include reasoning tokens depending on the endpoint.
help.tooltipDelay: Wait this many seconds while the pointer remains over a label before showing help. Moving away cancels the wait. Use any positive finite value. This affects the interface only, not character timers or API requests.
help.totalDuration: Recorded time for generation, including queue wait and provider streaming. It does not measure the character's subsequent cooldown or all paced publication time.
help.wordsPerPart: A longer response is split into parts of roughly this many whitespace-separated words. Other characters can speak between parts. The parts are generated together and cannot react to intervening messages.
help.workingContext: Optional application context budget in tokens. Zero uses the provider profile's configured capacity. A smaller value makes compaction happen sooner. Output and safety reserves must also fit inside the budget.
help.writingCorrections: Number of extra model generations requested because returned prose violated a global punctuation restriction. At most one correction is attempted. A second failure is reported rather than published.

settings.diagnostics.reasoningEffortBelo: Reasoning effort belongs to each provider profile. Hiding reasoning does not reduce inference effort. Estimates and reported token usage are labeled separately.
settings.diagnostics.reasoningStorageLim: Reasoning storage limit per request, in characters
settings.globalDefaultsApplyToExistingSe: Global defaults apply to existing sessions unless a session has its own override.
settings.interface.positiveDelay: The delay must be a positive number. The previous value was kept.
settings.interface.tooltipDelayHint: Saved automatically for this browser. Default 0.6 seconds. Keyboard focus, click, and tap open help immediately.

settings.memory.0UsesTheProviderSConfigu: 0 uses the provider's configured full context capacity.
settings.memory.checkpointFilesLiveUnder: Checkpoint files live under data/sessions/[session]/characters/[character]/. Failed compaction keeps the prior valid memory.
settings.memory.includeA24HourClockInMod: Include a 24-hour clock in model-visible observations
settings.memory.theFullTranscriptRemains: The full transcript remains on disk. Each character retains a private first-person memory and a recent observation tail.
settings.narrator.notableMomentsAreTheNa: Notable moments are the narrator's interpretations, linked to source messages. Quiet intervals do not need invented events.
settings.narrator.preparePeriodicRecapsW: Prepare periodic recaps while sessions run
settings.narrator.theNarratorObservesIts: The narrator observes. Its reports never become dialogue or character memory.
settings.prompts.appliesToEveryCharacter: Applies to every model request, including character turns, memory compaction, narrator recaps, and corrections. Scene overrides and saved worlds cannot replace these global rules. Required JSON syntax is preserved.
settings.prompts.characterInstructionsCa: Character instructions can use {name} and {word_limit}. Memory instructions can use {target_words}. Public dialogue is always treated as data.
settings.prompts.punctuationEnforcement: These restrictions are checked in returned prose fields. A violating response gets one correction attempt, then an explicit error if it still fails. JSON syntax and protocol identifiers stay valid.
settings.runtime.automaticallyResumeRunn: Automatically resume running worlds after a backend restart
settings.runtime.byDefaultABackendRestar: By default, a backend restart restores worlds paused. Closing the browser or navigating away never pauses a running session.
settings.runtime.eachCooldownSendsTheCur: Each cooldown sends the current board tail and that character's memory. The model may speak or return no response.
settings.runtime.minimumSecondsBetweenDe: Minimum seconds between delivered speech parts.
settings.runtime.sharedByDialogueMemoryA: Shared by dialogue, memory, and narration.
